title: The Guardian of the Gate, part 3
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: “Why, it is said that he never lets anyone come into his presence. I have been to the Emerald City many times, and it is a beautiful and wonderful place; but I have never been permitted to see the Great Oz, nor do I know of any living person who has seen him.”
“Does he never go out?” asked the Scarecrow.
“Never. He sits day after day in the great Throne Room of his Palace, and even those who wait upon him do not see him face to face.”
“What is he like?” asked the girl.

“That is hard to tell,” said the man thoughtfully. “You see, Oz is a Great Wizard, and can take on any form he wishes. So that some say he looks like a bird; and some say he looks like an elephant; and some say he looks like a cat. To others he appears as a beautiful fairy, or a brownie, or in any other form that pleases him. But who the real Oz is, when he is in his own form, no living person can tell.”
“That is very strange,” said Dorothy, “but we must try, in some way, to see him, or we shall have made our journey for nothing.”
“Why do you wish to see the terrible Oz?” asked the man.
“I want him to give me some brains,” said the Scarecrow eagerly.
“Oh, Oz could do that easily enough,” declared the man. “He has more brains than he needs.”
“And I want him to give me a heart,” said the Tin Woodman.
“That will not trouble him,” continued the man, “for Oz has a large collection of hearts, of all sizes and shapes.”
“And I want him to give me courage,” said the Cowardly Lion.
“Oz keeps a great pot of courage in his Throne Room,” said the man, “which he has covered with a golden plate, to keep it from running over. He will be glad to give you some.”

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is said about Oz letting people see him?
options: That he never lets anyone come into his presence
That he sees anyone who asks politely
That he sees only the people of the Emerald City
That he sees visitors once a year

questions.prompt: Per the passage, where does Oz spend his days?
options: In the great Throne Room of his Palace
Walking the streets of the city
In a tower above the green wall
Travelling through the four countries

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what forms is Oz said to take?
options: A bird, an elephant, a cat, a fairy, or a brownie
Only a bird or a cat, and nothing else
A Munchkin, a Winkie, or a Quadling
A wizard in a green robe and peaked hat

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what does the man say about Oz and brains?
options: That he has more brains than he needs
That he has none of his own to spare
That he keeps them locked in a box
That he has never given any away

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how is the pot of courage kept?
options: Covered with a golden plate to stop it running over
Buried beneath the floor of the Throne Room
Guarded by the Guardian of the Gates
Locked in a green box behind the throne

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why can nobody say what Oz really looks like?
options: He can take any form he wishes, so his own is unknown
He has never once left the Throne Room
Everyone who sees him is destroyed at once
The people are forbidden to describe him

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the man's own experience prove?
options: Even frequent visitors to the city have never seen Oz
Anyone who asks long enough is admitted in the end
The Wizard sees only those who bring him gifts
The Throne Room is open to all the green people

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does Dorothy insist they must try?
options: Otherwise the whole journey will have been for nothing
Otherwise the Wizard will be angry at their delay
Because the Witch of the North ordered her to
Because the man has promised to guide them

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that even those who wait upon him do not see him face to face?
options: Not even his own servants meet him directly
His servants see him only from a distance
His servants are chosen for their poor eyesight
He speaks to his servants through the Guardian

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: Oz is described as able to grant anything, but almost impossible to reach
Oz is shown to be an ordinary man like any other
The man offers to lead the party into the Throne Room
The travellers decide the Wizard is not worth seeking

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how often has the man been to the Emerald City?
options: Many times
Only once, long ago
Never in his life
Every year since boyhood

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what does the man say Oz has a large collection of?
options: Hearts of all sizes and shapes
Pots of courage and brains
Spectacles with green glasses
Golden keys to the city gates

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the man describe the Emerald City itself?
options: A beautiful and wonderful place
A cold and frightening place
A city nobody may enter
A ruin behind a green wall

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how does the man answer each of the three requests?
options: He treats every one of them as easy for Oz to grant
He warns that Oz has never granted any of them
He says only the brains could possibly be given
He refuses to discuss what Oz can and cannot do

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what makes the difficulty the travellers face?
options: Not what they ask for, but getting to ask it at all
That none of them knows the way to the palace
That the Wizard grants only one wish a year
That the Guardian of the Gates dislikes strangers

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does permitted mean?
options: Allowed
Invited
Forced
Paid

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A hopeful account of what Oz can give, set against how unreachable he is
A warning that Oz destroys everyone who dares approach him
A description of the four shapes the Wizard usually takes
An offer to take the travellers into the city the next day
